subject: Student case study
body:
Hello {player_name},
I am a graduate student writing a case study on analytics teams in mid-sized firms. Could I ask a few general questions about your tooling?[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: An unknown outsider asking about internal tools; no approved research request exists
Asks which security tools you use
tells.text: Which cloud and VPN products does your team use?
Could you also forward the org chart?

explanation: Reconnaissance. Harmless-sounding answers build a map of your systems for later attacks.

body: Hi, this is a courtesy check from Corvane Cloud support. We are updating our records and want to confirm which people on your team manage admin accounts.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: The vendor contacted you unprompted and there is no open support case
Asks for names and usernames of admins
tells.text: Could you list the names and usernames they sign in with?
It only takes a minute, no need to check with your manager.

explanation: A routine-sounding vendor check is used to identify the people with the most access.

subject: Call transcript
body: Caller: 'Hi, Marcus from Corvane Cloud support. You opened a ticket last week about slow dashboards. To close it I need remote access to your machine. Can you read me the access code on your screen?[[t3]][[t5]]'

tells.flag: You never opened that ticket and there is no matching ticket in the helpdesk
Refuses to give a verifiable ticket number now
tells.text: I will text you the ticket number afterwards.

tells.flag: Asks you to install unknown software
tells.text: Please also install the small helper tool I am about to describe.

explanation: A convincing technical story ('your ticket') justifies remote access. Always check the ticket yourself via the known helpdesk first.

subject: Case C-77310 - still open
body: Following up on case C-77310. We cannot close it without remote access, and your dashboards may go offline from tomorrow.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: The case number does not exist in your helpdesk, and the sender domain is not the vendor's known address
Asks you to approve access without checking
tells.text: Please approve the access request now.

tells.flag: Asks for an admin password by email
tells.text: Or reply with your admin password so we can do it overnight.

explanation: After rapport and a pretext, a consequence is added. A made-up case number is the thread to pull on.
